title: Remove Stones to Minimize the Total
summary: Given an array piles where piles[i] is the number of stones in the i-th pile, and an integer k, perform exactly k operations by removing floor(piles[i] / 2) stones from any pile.
statement: Given an array piles where piles[i] is the number of stones in the i-th pile, and an integer k, perform exactly k operations by removing floor(piles[i] / 2) stones from any pile. Return the smallest total number of stones remaining after k operations, where floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x.
constraints: piles has 1 through 100000 positive counts, each at most 10000.
Each operation chooses one current pile and removes floor(pile/2), leaving ceil(pile/2); perform exactly k operations.
hints: One operation removes more stones from a larger pile, so always choose the current maximum.
Store negative pile sizes in a min-heap; pop the largest, replace it with ceil(pile/2), and repeat k times.
heapify negatives; repeat: p=-pop; push(-(p-p//2)); return -sum(heap).
If an operation chose a smaller pile while a larger existed, swapping that operation to the larger removes at least as many now and cannot reduce future options, proving the greedy choice.
